title: γ-aminobutyric acid is associated with calcium, reactive oxygen species, and nitric oxide responses and enhanced cadmium tolerance in  Salvadora persica

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《γ-aminobutyric acid is associated with calcium, reactive oxygen species, and nitric oxide responses and enhanced cadmium tolerance in  Salvadora persica》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · s0005-p4】Therefore, we evaluated whether exogenous GABA-associated Cd protection coincided with a feedback-linked Ca2+-ROS-NO response and downstream thiol, ionic, photosynthetic, phenolic, and flavonoid outcomes. The objectives were (i) to identify a sub-lethal Cd dose and an effective GABA concentration; (ii) to compare Ca2+-sensitive and NO-associated relative fluorescence responses and H₂O₂ at five defined times; (iii) to assess responses to LaCl₃, EGTA, DPI, DMTU, and cPTIO; and (iv) to characterize multivariate associations using multiplicity-controlled univariate tests, Pearson correlations, and principal component analysis. No confirmatory path analysis objective was retained because the available design did not support the estimation and reporting of a fully specified path model with coefficients and global fit statistics.

【Introduction · s0005-p1】γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA) is a four-carbon non-protein amino acid that functions as a metabolic intermediate and stress signal. Recent evidence has shown that GABA regulates anion transport, the membrane potential, stomatal behavior, respiratory metabolism, antioxidant capacity, osmotic adjustment, and ion homeostasis under environmental stress 1-8 . Its signaling role is especially relevant to metal toxicity because early Ca2+ and redox responses may accompany protection, although their timing alone cannot establish whether GABA initiates them 9-12 . Calcium (Ca2+) is one of the first messengers activated after stress perception. The amplitude, duration, and spatial distribution of cytosolic Ca2+ form stimulus-specific signatures that are decoded by Ca2+-binding proteins and protein kinases. 13-15 These decoders activate respiratory burst oxidase homologs at the plasma membrane, connecting Ca2+ signals with reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and rapid root-to-shoot communication. 16-18 M​easurements at defined times are required to assess whether GABA treatment is associated with altered Ca2+-sensitive fluorescence during acclimation.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《γ-aminobutyric acid is associated with calcium, reactive oxygen species, and nitric oxide responses and enhanced cadmium tolerance in  Salvadora persica》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Growth substrate characterization and growth-condition methods · s0006-s2002-p1】Plastic pots (18 cm top diameter, 16 cm height) were filled with 3.0 kg of a sand-loam substrate (2:1 v/v) sieved through a 2-mm mesh. The physicochemical properties of the substrate are listed in Table 1. The background Cd concentration was below 0.35 mg kg−1, confirming that the substrate was not pre-contaminated and that all measured Cd could be attributed to the applied treatments. Substrate pH and electrical conductivity were determined in a 1:2.5 (w/v) suspension, organic carbon by the Walkley‒Black procedure, total nitrogen by the Kjeldahl method, available phosphorus by the Olsen method, and extractable potassium by ammonium acetate extraction followed by flame photometry. Pseudo-total Cd and Pb were extracted in aqua regia and quantified by atomic absorption spectrophotometry. The experiment was carried out in a controlled-environment glasshouse at the Department of Botany, The Women University Multan (30.20° N, 71.47° E), at 30 ± 2 °C d/22 ± 2 °C night, 60 ± 5% relative humidity, a 14-h photoperiod, and a photosynthetic photon flux density of 650 μmol m−2 s at the canopy level supplied by daylight supplemented with LED panels. Pots were watered to 70% of water-holding capacity by weight every second day and re-randomized on the bench weekly to remove positional effects.

【Experimental design and pharmacological-dissection method · s0006-s2005-p1】The main experiment comprised 11 treatments in a completely randomized design, with one plant per pot and five independently randomized pots per treatment (n = 55 experimental units). The pots were not divided among the treatments. For destructive sampling of signaling measurements, separate treatment-assigned pots were harvested at each sampling time. The regions of interest within a plant were considered technical subsamples and were averaged before analysis. Thus, the pot/plant mean, rather than an image region, was the unit of inference. Core treatments and pharmacological perturbations were applied as described below.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《γ-aminobutyric acid is associated with calcium, reactive oxygen species, and nitric oxide responses and enhanced cadmium tolerance in  Salvadora persica》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · s0009-p1】Exogenous GABA mitigated cadmium toxicity in Salvadora persica in association with differences in Ca2+-sensitive and NO-associated relative fluorescence responses and H₂O₂ at the five sampled times. Treatment effects on the method-supported endpoint outcomes were evaluated with pot/plant as the experimental unit and specified in a 37-outcome Benjamini–Hochberg family; exact adjusted q-values and residual diagnostics are unavailable for verification. The observed responses coincided with stronger thiol/redox defenses, reduced Cd accumulation and translocation, improved leaf photosynthetic measurements and growth at the measured endpoint, and higher total phenolic and flavonoid concentrations. The correlation and PCA results describe multivariate associations only. The attenuation by LaCl₃, EGTA, DPI, DMTU, and cPTIO shows the sensitivity of the GABA-associated phenotype to the tested compounds, while the effects of DPI, DMTU, and cPTIO on the Ca2+-sensitive peak suggest feedback. These interventions do not establish that GABA acts upstream, through a linear pathway, or compound-specific effects. Figure 11 presents a conceptual hypothesis, not a fitted path model. Without documented inhibitor phytotoxicity screening, inhibitor-only controls, or a rescue experiment, these findings cannot distinguish pathway perturbation from compound toxicity or off-target effects.

【Conclusion · abstract-4-1】GABA was associated with improved Cd tolerance and differences in sampled fluorescence, H₂O₂, and thiol responses. These data cannot establish a continuous signaling sequence, upstream GABA action, or target-specific pharmacological effects. The attenuation is compatible with network involvement and feedback, but pathway direction and pharmacological specificity require inhibitor-only controls, rescue experiments, and independent, well-controlled temporal validation in future studies.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《γ-aminobutyric acid is associated with calcium, reactive oxygen species, and nitric oxide responses and enhanced cadmium tolerance in  Salvadora persica》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · f0001】Figure 1. Effects of cadmium (Cd) and γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) on (a) shoot dry weight, (b) root dry weight, (c) lipid peroxidation measured as malondialdehyde (MDA), (d) maximum quantum efficiency of photosystem II (F v/F m), and (e) Cd tolerance index in Salvadora persica. C, untreated control; Cd, Cd treatment; Cd+G₀.₂₅, Cd with 0.25 mM GABA; Cd+GABA, Cd with the study’s principal GABA dose; Cd+G₁.₀, Cd with 1.0 mM GABA. The bars show means with error bars. Different letters above the bars indicate statistically significant differences among the treatments.

【Figure 2. · f0002】Figure 2. Relative fluorescence and H₂O₂ responses of Salvadora persica to Cd and GABA at five sampling times: Ca2+-sensitive Fluo-3 AM relative fluorescence response in (a) root tips and (b) leaf mesophyll, H₂O₂ in (c) roots and (d) leaves, and NO-associated DAF-FM DA relative fluorescence response in (e) roots and (f) leaves at 0, 30, 180, 360, and 1440 min after application. The treatments were: control (C), 0.5 mM GABA alone, 50 mg Cd kg−1 (Cd), and Cd+0.5 mM GABA. Symbols represent the mean ± standard error of five biological replicates; the x-axis is ordinal. The nominal 0-min sample was collected within 60 s after application and was not a true baseline. RFU values are relative, non-ratiometric signals and should not be interpreted as absolute Ca2+ or NO concentrations; the sparse sampling identifies observed maxima but not exact peak times or continuous kinetics.

【Figure 3. · f0003】Figure 3. Effects of GABA and pharmacological treatments under Cd stress on (a) root and (b) leaf Ca2+ relative fluorescence responses at 30 min; (c) root and (d) leaf H₂O₂ at 180 min; (e) root and (f) leaf NO relative fluorescence responses at 360 min; (g) lipid peroxidation at 24 h; and (h) shoot dry weight. C, untreated control; GABA, γ-aminobutyric acid; LaCl₃, lanthanum chloride; EGTA, ethylene glycol tetraacetic acid; DPI, diphenyleneiodonium; DMTU, dimethylthiourea; cPTIO, nitric oxide scavenger. The bars represent treatment means with error bars. Different letters above the bars indicate the statistical groupings shown in the figure. The Ca2+ and NO values are relative fluorescence units (RFU), not calibrated concentrations. Because these inhibitors are not target-specific, their effects do not establish a linear or exclusively on-target Ca2+–ROS–NO pathway.
